headline: Revolut handed customer passports and financial records to fraudsters who submitted emergency data requests from a working government email account, the sharpest example of a day in which impersonated authority and freshly disclosed developer-infrastructure flaws both paid off.

emerging_trends.text: Criminals now borrow the authority of the state itself, writing to Revolut from a legitimate government email domain to pry loose customer passports while other crews stand up hundreds of counterfeit government websites across Central Asia to farm contact details for follow-up phone and email fraud.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Revolut and Telus Disclose Customer Data Theft

emerging_trends.text: Chinese operators convert newly disclosed developer-infrastructure bugs into campaigns within days, as Red Heron shows by scanning 1,386 Gitea instances and breaking into 13 organizations, a pattern that also runs through the JFrog Artifactory backdoors and the GitLab commits API flaw CISA cataloged this week.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Red Heron Exploits Gitea RCE Across Six Countries

emerging_trends.text: The argument over who restrains AI reached governments today, with Dario Amodei asking the industry to slow frontier model improvement, Beijing's Ministry of Foreign Affairs answering his essay, and enterprise security leaders wrestling with agents that hold far more privilege than their tasks require.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Amodei Calls for Control as Beijing Answers

topics.title: Revolut and Telus Disclose Customer Data Theft
topics.latest_developments: The Record reported on September 14, 2026 that the fraudsters who extracted Revolut customer records submitted emergency data requests from a working government email account, sharpening the disclosure Revolut confirmed on Saturday, September 12, 2026, and Telus warned subscribers the same day that intruders used stolen credentials across a multi-month campaign to reach personal data and billing records.
topics.summary: The Revolut notification to affected customers lists birth dates, postal and email addresses, phone numbers, and copies of identity documents including passports, and the company told TechCrunch a limited number of customers lost data and that it contacted each of them directly. Customers of both companies should treat unsolicited contact referencing their account details as fraud and watch for identity theft.

sources.title: Revolut discloses data breach exposing financial info, passports
Revolut handed customer data to fraudsters using government email account
What we know about the Revolut data breach so far
Telus Warns Customers of Account Breaches

topics.title: Amodei Calls for Control as Beijing Answers
topics.latest_developments: Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, told the industry on September 14, 2026 to slow frontier model improvement so that security and risk prevention catch up, and China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs replied to his essay urging limits on Chinese AI development by saying all parties should work together on the technology.
topics.summary: Amodei's argument extends the warning he gave a day earlier that an AI system could soon direct a swarm of agents across the internet, and it lands as Anthropic's own misuse report documents a cell in northern Yemen that used Claude on three weapons development programs, among them a guided rocket and a ballistic missile with a stated range above 2,000 kilometers. Enterprises weighing frontier model deployments should read the safety timeline as contested and plan controls that do not depend on vendor restraint.

sources.title: Anthropic CEO: Time to Shift From Improving to Controlling AI
Beijing Hits Back at Anthropic CEO's Call to Curb China's AI Development
Using AI for Weapons Development
New Warnings About the Risks of AI to Humanity Revive a Long-Running Debate

topics.title: September Windows Updates Break Remote Desktop and USB Audio
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft confirmed on September 14, 2026 that its September 2026 security updates knock out Remote Desktop Services on Windows Server, matching four days of administrator reports, and acknowledged a second regression in which USB audio devices fail after the KB5124008 and KB5124012 updates.
topics.summary: The Remote Desktop failures block user connections on Windows Server 2019, 2022, and 2025, and some hosts recover only after a hard reset. Administrators running the September rollup should test remote access and audio hardware before broad deployment and watch Microsoft's release health dashboard for the fixes.

sources.title: Microsoft: September updates cause RDS failures on Windows Server
Microsoft: September updates break audio on some Windows PCs
Microsoft's Patching

topics.title: Deepfake Sites Target More Than 100 European Politicians
topics.latest_developments: Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg announced on September 14, 2026 that his office seized 12 celebrity deepfake websites carrying hyper-realistic sexual imagery of roughly 1,200 people, the largest legal action yet against such sites, hours after Wired published an analysis of 160 deepfake websites that found more than 100 politicians from 22 countries in Europe on them, with women accounting for nearly every target.
topics.summary: The sites run openly and pull public images of serving politicians and celebrities into explicit video and photographs. Bragg's seizures give prosecutors a template, and the European totals hand regulators a concrete test of the push to hold platforms and tool makers accountable for synthetic sexual imagery.

sources.title: Sexually Explicit Deepfake Sites Target 100-Plus Politicians in Europe
New York Seizes 12 Celebrity Deepfake Websites
New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites

topics.title: Third JFrog Artifactory Flaw Joins Backdoor Campaign
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 14, 2026 that attackers chain three JFrog Artifactory vulnerabilities, one more than the pair CISA cataloged on September 11, to bypass authentication and raise their privileges to administrator before planting a backdoor.
topics.summary: CISA already lists the incorrect authorization bug CVE-2026-42016 and the improper authentication bug CVE-2026-42018 as actively exploited, and Wiz dated the campaign against self-hosted Artifactory servers from August 15 through September 8, 2026, finding it reached only operators who had skipped JFrog's earlier fixes. Anyone running Artifactory on their own hardware should install every available update and hunt for a Rust backdoor and unfamiliar administrator accounts.

sources.title: Three JFrog Artifactory Flaws Exploited for Backdoor Deployment
CISA: Hackers now exploit max severity GitLab flaw in attacks

topics.title: Chinese Hackers Ride Sogou Flaw to GrayRabbit
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 14, 2026 that CVE-2026-51990 in Tencent's Sogou Input Method for Windows hands attackers remote code execution from a single click, the mechanism behind the China-aligned espionage campaign that BleepingComputer tied a day earlier to the GrayRabbit backdoor.
topics.summary: Sogou Input Method ranks among the most widely installed tools for typing Chinese characters on Windows, and operators start each intrusion with a crafted link that plants GrayRabbit carrying the logged-in user's full rights. Anyone running Sogou Input Method should update it or pull it off corporate machines.

sources.title: Chinese Hackers Exploit Critical Tencent Software Flaw for One-Click Code Execution
Hackers exploit Tencent app flaw to deploy GrayRabbit malware

topics.title: CISOs Fight Over-Privileged AI Agents as AWS Measures False Positives
topics.latest_developments: Amazon Web Services released its Deception Benchmark publicly on September 14, 2026, a dataset and evaluation process that scores how well AI models separate genuine vulnerabilities from code that merely looks risky, and found the models piling up false positives; SecurityWeek reported the same day that security leaders are struggling to rein in over-privileged agents without stripping out the value those agents deliver.
topics.summary: Security teams now point AI at vulnerability triage, penetration testing, threat modeling, incident response, and code review, and every false positive adds work for the humans reviewing the output. Teams should benchmark any model before they trust its findings and scope agent permissions to the narrowest set of systems each task requires.

sources.title: AWS puts AI vulnerability detection to the test, and false positives pile up
CISOs Race to Control AI Agents Without Destroying Their Value

topics.title: Red Heron Exploits Gitea RCE Across Six Countries
topics.latest_developments: Acronis Threat Research Unit reported on September 14, 2026 that the Chinese threat actor it tracks as Red Heron turned a recently disclosed Gitea remote code execution flaw against internet-facing servers within days, scanning 1,386 Gitea instances in seven countries, keeping a separate list of 477 systems in Taiwan, and breaking into 13 organizations across six countries.
topics.summary: Gitea is self-hosted Git software that many engineering teams run on their own servers, which puts source code, build credentials, and deployment keys behind a single internet-facing application. Anyone operating Gitea should patch immediately, pull the server off the public internet, and review repositories and access tokens for tampering.

sources.title: Red Heron Exploits Gitea RCE to Compromise 13 Organizations Across Six Countries

topics.title: ConnectWise Patches Wormable ScreenConnect Flaw
topics.latest_developments: ConnectWise released the fix on September 14, 2026 for the ScreenConnect file transfer flaw it had covered with temporary mitigations a week earlier, closing a hole that lets an attacker send files through an active remote session and execute them without authorization.
topics.summary: Huntress traced three unrelated intrusions in which backdoored ScreenConnect instances pushed a four-stage Visual Basic Script payload to every newly connected host, a spread that started with a Quick Assist tech-support scam, a phishing-delivered MSI installer, and a fake update. The flaw reaches both the ConnectWise cloud service and on-premises installations, so every operator should apply the patch and audit recent session file transfers.

sources.title: ConnectWise Patches ScreenConnect Vulnerability Exploited in Worm-Like Attacks

topics.title: ENISA Opens the Cyber Resilience Act Reporting Portal
topics.latest_developments: The EU Agency for Cybersecurity switched on the Cyber Resilience Act's Single Reporting Platform on September 11, 2026, the day the law's reporting duties began binding manufacturers, and now runs the portal day to day under Article 16(1) of the act.
topics.summary: Any company placing a product with digital elements on the European Union market reports actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through that single portal, and the act gives 24 hours from discovery to notify authorities. Product and legal teams selling into the European Union should register with the platform and rehearse the one-day clock.

sources.title: ENISA launched the CRA Single Reporting Platform for actively exploited vulnerabilities

business_politics.title: Trump Says Kyiv and Moscow Agreed to an Energy Truce
business_politics.latest_developments: President Trump announced Monday, September 14, that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking each other's energy infrastructure, an announcement that caught Kyiv off guard.
business_politics.summary: Trump spent Sunday pressing Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries, blaming them for record diesel prices, and earlier attempts to spare power plants and refineries fell apart. Russian drones and missiles are meanwhile battering Ukraine's railway system, and U.S. retail diesel set a record last week above $6 a gallon as Middle East supply disruptions piled up.

business_politics.title: Oil Reaches $108 as Riyadh Quits the Hormuz Talks
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent held at $109 a barrel Monday, September 14, with Saudi Arabia racing to repair the drone-damaged East-West pipeline, Houthi forces seizing two more strategic Red Sea islands, and Riyadh out of the regional talks to de-escalate the Strait of Hormuz standoff.
business_politics.summary: The East-West line carries crude from Saudi Arabia's eastern fields to the Red Sea and served as the main workaround for the blocked Strait of Hormuz. Houthi fighters now hold the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint as well, putting both of the region's vital energy corridors under the sway of Iran and its allies, and gas traders have moved to pricing an outage that runs through the winter.

business_politics.title: Warsh Faces Trump Over Wednesday's Rate Increase
business_politics.latest_developments: The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5% Monday, September 14, the first time since 2023, and the dollar strengthened and gold fell as traders positioned for Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh to raise rates Wednesday over President Trump's objections.
business_politics.summary: The Federal Reserve meets September 16 and the Bank of Japan follows September 18, with both expected to tighten, the Fed for the first time in years. Mohamed El-Erian argues that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has misdiagnosed the bond selloff as a passing fever, and Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda faces competing pressure from Tokyo and Washington.

business_politics.title: A Call to Slow AI Knocks Down Tech Shares Worldwide
business_politics.latest_developments: Memory-chip makers and Nvidia led a global selloff Monday, September 14, after Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei's weekend essay warning against a race to the bottom in model development, though the Nasdaq pared its early losses through the session as Steve Bannon and Senator Bernie Sanders joined to demand stronger regulation and Congress began weighing its own response.
business_politics.summary: Anthropic, the maker of Claude, told investors it expects a second straight profitable quarter as it prepares an initial public offering that could value it near $2 trillion. Its schism with OpenAI has driven the industry's sprint toward ever more powerful systems, and the market read Amodei's plea for restraint as a threat to the earnings the buildout promises.

business.title: Woda Cooper Gets $4.85 Million From the URA
business.latest_developments: The Urban Redevelopment Authority board voted 4-0, with one member absent, to approve two loans totaling $4.85 million for Woda Cooper Cos.' next conversion of a downtown Pittsburgh building into apartments, WPXI reported Monday, September 14.
business.summary: Woda Cooper Cos. builds and manages affordable housing and has already worked on downtown Pittsburgh office-to-residential conversions. The URA lends city money to close the financing gaps on these projects, and this was the board's first action after the August recess in city public meetings.

sources.title: Woda Cooper secures $4.85M in URA funding for its next downtown Pittsburgh residential conversion

business.title: Citizens Leaves the Giant Eagle for Walnut Street
business.latest_developments: Citizens filed with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on September 4 to close its Shadyside branch inside the Giant Eagle at 5550 Centre Avenue and move it to a standalone storefront at 5508 Walnut Street, WPXI reported Monday, September 14.
business.summary: The bank told WPXI it is targeting late in the fourth quarter of 2026 or early 2027 for the move. The Walnut Street space last housed an Apple Store, and Citizens trades a supermarket kiosk for a larger presence on Shadyside's main shopping street.

sources.title: Retail shuffle: Citizens snags former Apple Store space for new standalone location

business.title: Alcoa Nears a Data Center Sale
business.latest_developments: Alcoa Chief Financial Officer Molly Beerman said the Pittsburgh-based manufacturer is in talks to sell its closed Messina East smelter in Messina, New York, for use as a data center site, WPXI reported Monday, September 14.
business.summary: Alcoa shut the Messina East smelter and has looked for a buyer since. Data center developers keep buying old aluminum and coal sites for the heavy electrical connections already built into them, the same logic behind Project Phoenix, the data center that broke ground beside a former coal plant campus in Beaver County last week.

sources.title: Alcoa nears sale for data center location

business.title: Heating Bills Climb Into Winter
business.latest_developments: WTAE reported Monday, September 14, that the average American household will spend $1,030 on heat this winter, an increase that arrives with household budgets already stretched.
business.summary: The forecast lands on a region that watched retail diesel pass $6 a gallon Friday, September 11, as the Middle East conflict squeezed global fuel supply. Families with no slack left in their budgets face trade-offs between heat and other bills.

sources.title: 'No room left in their budgets': US heating bills expected to rise this winter

business.title: be.wild.er Farm Becomes a Cooperative
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 14, that be.wild.er, the Natrona Heights farm now in its tenth year, has converted to a cooperative.
business.summary: Small farms around the country have turned to shared ownership to spread the cost and risk of land, equipment, and labor across their workers. be.wild.er sells online and joins that shift in the Pittsburgh region.

sources.title: Some small farms are becoming co-ops. Add Pittsburgh's be.wild.er to the list

business.title: DeFoor Audits the Medical Marijuana Program
business.latest_developments: Pennsylvania Auditor General Timothy L. DeFoor released a performance audit Sunday, September 13, of the Department of Health's handling of the state Medical Marijuana Program.
business.summary: The Department of Health licenses the growers, processors, and dispensaries that serve Pennsylvania's registered medical cannabis patients, and the auditor general's office reviews how it runs that program. The findings bear on operators across Western Pennsylvania and on the patients who buy from them.

sources.title: Pennsylvania Auditor General releases performance audit of state's medical marijuana program

around_town.title: EPA Scraps Power Plant Carbon Limits
around_town.latest_developments: The Environmental Protection Agency moved Monday, September 14, to repeal the rules limiting greenhouse gas emissions from power plants burning coal and natural gas.
around_town.summary: Administrator Lee Zeldin says the repeal removes billions of dollars in costs from the industry and will unleash American energy. Pennsylvania runs one of the largest coal and gas generating fleets in the country and exports power across the PJM grid, so the change reaches plants throughout Western Pennsylvania.

sources.title: EPA eliminates rule that limits planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants
Trump EPA is to eliminate rule that limits planet-warming greenhouse gas emissions from power plants

around_town.title: Penn State Clears the Way to Sell Campuses
around_town.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Monday, September 14, that legislation passed quietly in Harrisburg lets Penn State proceed with potential sales of campuses it is closing, among them Penn State Shenango and Penn State Wilkes-Barre.
around_town.summary: Penn State decided to shut several of its Commonwealth campuses, including Shenango in New Castle, Lawrence County. The new law governs what the university may do with those buildings and grounds once the students leave, which determines what the host communities get in their place.

sources.title: How quietly passed legislation will allow Penn State to move forward with potential campus sales

around_town.title: Measles Deaths Reach Three in Pennsylvania
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Monday, September 14, that the Jefferson County woman who died of measles complications had several chronic respiratory conditions and is the first adult among the state's three measles-related deaths this year.
around_town.summary: The two earlier deaths involved infants, and a coroner confirmed last week that the virus itself caused one of them. Pennsylvania counted 676 measles cases as of Friday, September 11, the largest outbreak in the country this year.

sources.title: Jefferson County measles-related death marks 1st adult fatality in statewide outbreak

around_town.title: A Sinkhole Swallows a South Strabane Fire Station Lot
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported Monday, September 14, that flash flooding opened a 40-foot sinkhole under a fire station parking lot in South Strabane Township, Washington County, with repairs estimated as high as $750,000.
around_town.summary: The collapse follows the storms that filled streets in the city of Washington and pushed the city to declare a state of emergency on Saturday, September 12. The repair bill falls on a volunteer department's home station in a township of roughly 9,000 people southeast of Pittsburgh.

sources.title: Washington County fire station parking lot collapses into 40-foot sinkhole after flash flooding

around_town.title: Rabies Baits Drop From Helicopters This Week
around_town.latest_developments: The U.S. Department of Agriculture began distributing oral rabies vaccine baits by helicopter across Western Pennsylvania this week, WPXI reported Monday, September 14.
around_town.summary: The agency drops the baits each year to vaccinate raccoons and other wildlife and hold the rabies front line along the Appalachians. Residents who find the packets should leave them alone and keep pets away.

sources.title: Rabies vaccine baits to be distributed via helicopter across Western Pennsylvania

around_town.title: County Rebuilds Its Addiction Treatment System
around_town.latest_developments: The Allegheny County Department of Human Services announced an initiative Sunday, September 13, to restructure how the county delivers drug and alcohol treatment.
around_town.summary: The department funds and coordinates the providers that treat county residents for substance use disorder, and the restructuring changes how those services fit together. It touches the treatment options available to families across Allegheny County.

sources.title: Allegheny County DHS to restructure drug, alcohol treatment system

around_town.title: Shapiro Holds a 38-to-1 Cash Lead
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource laid out Monday, September 14, the scale of Governor Josh Shapiro's fundraising advantage over Republican challenger Stacy Garrity, a 38-to-1 lead in cash on hand as of June, much of it raised outside Pennsylvania.
around_town.summary: Shapiro, the Democratic incumbent, faces Garrity, the state treasurer, in the November 3 election for governor. PublicSource will track contributions in the race through Election Day.

sources.title: Here's what Shapiro's huge edge over Garrity in national campaign contributions looks like

around_town.title: A Cool, Clear Start to the Week
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE forecast a comfortable, bright Monday, September 14, across Western Pennsylvania behind Sunday's storm line, with warmth and humidity building back by midweek.
around_town.summary: A cold front swept the region Sunday with damaging wind, hail, and heavy rain through Allegheny, Butler, and Beaver counties. The break in the heat lasts only a couple of days.

sources.title: Western PA: Comfortable and bright to kick off the week
Western Pennsylvania gets brief fall cool down after Sunday storms

events.title: Clothesline Sale Returns to Sewickley Academy
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported Monday, September 14, that Sewickley Academy's annual Clothesline Sale runs daily from Thursday, September 17, through Monday, September 21.
events.summary: The school holds the secondhand sale each year in Snyder Gym on the Sewickley Academy campus in Sewickley, Allegheny County.

sources.title: Sewickley Academy Clothesline sale returns

around_teams.title: Greensboro's Prospects Carry a Playoff Run
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's MiLB Monday column on September 14 reported that the Pirates' best young hitters, outfielder Edward Florentino among them, are driving a playoff run at the organization's Greensboro affiliate.
around_teams.summary: The Greensboro Grasshoppers play in the High-A South Atlantic League and hold much of the talent the Pirates expect to promote over the next two seasons. The column tracks those prospects each week as the minor league postseason runs past the end of the major league schedule.

sources.title: MiLB Monday: Top prospects are shining during Greensboro's playoff run

around_teams.title: The Trade Deadline Comes Back to Bite the Pirates
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Off The Bat column argued Monday, September 14, that the Pirates' choices at this year's trade deadline should haunt the front office as the club's playoff hopes slip away.
around_teams.summary: Pittsburgh sold at the deadline and then played well enough down the stretch to stay on the edge of the wild card race, a late push that manager Don Kelly kept alive by avoiding a sweep at Wrigley Field on Sunday. The Pirates open their final homestand at PNC Park this week.

sources.title: Off The Bat: The Pirates' trade deadline decisions should haunt them as the playoffs slip away

around_teams.title: The Bill for Porter's Standoff Comes Later
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's Week 1 analysis, published Monday, September 14, concluded that the Steelers got through the opener without cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and warned that his absence will start to hurt soon.
around_teams.summary: Porter sat out Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons with his contract unresolved, and sources told the Post-Gazette he is healthy enough to play. The Steelers travel to face the New England Patriots on Sunday.

sources.title: Steelers Week 1 analysis: Joey Porter Jr.'s absence wasn't felt on Sunday, but it could be soon
Joey Porter Jr. was ruled out for the Steelers' opener, but sources say he is healthy enough to play

around_teams.title: Brisker's Hometown Debut
around_teams.latest_developments: Safety Jaquan Brisker intercepted a pass in his first game for the Steelers on Sunday, September 13, and the Post-Gazette's notebook made it the centerpiece of the defense's day alongside Cam Heyward and kicker Chris Boswell.
around_teams.summary: Brisker, a Western Pennsylvania native, signed with Pittsburgh this offseason after his run with the Chicago Bears, and he took the field at Acrisure Stadium for the first time as a Steeler in Mike McCarthy's head coaching debut.

sources.title: Steelers notebook: With a big play, Jaquan Brisker makes his hometown debut memorable

around_teams.title: Highsmith's Sack Sealed It
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette broke down late Sunday, September 13, the Alex Highsmith sack that closed out the Steelers' win over the Atlanta Falcons, the second defensive play that decided the game.
around_teams.summary: Highsmith and T.J. Watt both drew A-plus grades in the paper's report card on the opener, with Watt's pick-six the other turning point. The two outside linebackers carried a defense that head coach Mike McCarthy plans to rotate more heavily this season.

sources.title: Inside the other big defensive play that secured the Steelers their Week 1 win

team_usa.title: Macario's Season Ends in San Diego
team_usa.latest_developments: San Diego Wave FC placed United States forward Catarina Macario on the NWSL's season-ending injury list Monday, September 14, over a continuing knee problem.
team_usa.summary: Macario has scored for the United States women's national team since her debut in 2021, and knee injuries have repeatedly interrupted her career. The Wave now finish the NWSL season without her.

sources.title: Wave put USWNT's Macario on season-ending list

team_usa.title: Sullivan Scores Twice Before the Squad Reveal
team_usa.latest_developments: Philadelphia Union midfielder Cavan Sullivan scored twice and set up another goal in a 5-0 win over San Diego on Sunday, September 13, his first two-goal game in Major League Soccer, days ahead of a United States men's roster announcement.
team_usa.summary: Sullivan is the teenage Union midfielder United States coach Mauricio Pochettino asked fans to be patient with last week, alongside New York Red Bulls forward Julian Hall. The performance lands just as Pochettino names his next squad.

sources.title: Cavan Sullivan nets 2 ahead of U.S. squad reveal

team_usa.title: Team USA Credits Stewart for the Title Run
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Monday, September 14, that players and staff on the United States women's team pointed to Breanna Stewart as the force behind the fifth straight FIBA World Cup title, calling her the program's greatest winner.
team_usa.summary: The United States beat France in the final in Germany on Sunday, September 13, a rematch of the 2024 Olympic gold medal game, with Stewart scoring 22 points under coach Kara Lawson. Spain took the bronze medal, beating host Germany 81-58.

sources.title: 'Greatest winner' Stewart guides U.S. to fifth straight World Cup title

team_usa.title: Rodman Leaves a Spirit Loss for the US Open
team_usa.latest_developments: Trinity Rodman flew from the Washington Spirit's 3-0 defeat straight to Flushing Meadows to watch Ben Shelton play the US Open final, ESPN reported Monday, September 14.
team_usa.summary: Rodman, a United States women's national team winger and Olympic gold medalist, plays for the Spirit, whose loss dropped the club in ESPN's NWSL Power Rankings as Gotham FC took over the top spot. Shelton, an American, reached his first US Open final.
